messages:
marco: Heads-up: need to lock down launch criteria for enterprise evidence packaging + BYOK handshake before the roadmap review. Main open items: export format, signed integrity manifest, retention-cost UX, and what happens when a customer revokes a key.

anya: From legal: exports must be verifiable (detached signature + manifest), and chain-of-custody metadata attached. Need retention escalation process for legal holds.

li: Infra constraints: producing a fully-searchable 7y index is expensive. We should define a tiered export (searchable vs archived blob) and explicit rehydrate SLAs.

marco: Proposal: default export = tar.gz of evidence + manifest.json + sig.asc. Provide both quick-search bundle (90d) and archive bundle (cold).

sec-eng: Security asks: manifest must include key id, signing algorithm, key provenance, and a proof-of-rotation chain. If BYOK key is revoked, exports signed earlier must remain verifiable (so detached sigs are required).

product-bot: note: previous thread recommended 90/730/3650 retention tiers. need explicit acceptance tests for rehydrate time.

li: Acceptance tests we need:
- export integrity verification (validate signatures)
- rehydrate flow (cold -> warm -> searchable) under 48h in 95th pct
- legal-hold toggle preserves objects and prevents deletion

diane: Ops: runbook + oncall playbook required for revocation incidents. Also want a tenant-facing cost estimator: show estimated monthly cost delta when changing hot/warm thresholds. Less escalations that way.

anya: Legal-hold detail: the API must allow a tenant or Redwood legal to add a hold with reason + start_ts + optional end_ts, which suspends deletion and flags exports for priority retrieval.

marco: UX idea: show effective retention window and a cost delta slider. Also warn when BYOK enforces customer-side rotation (it may break auto-key rotation).

sec-eng: Clarify escrow: are we offering managed escrow for BYOK? If yes, require attestation logs and KMS access policies. If not, document recovery limitations.

li: Suggestion: MVP supports optional managed-escrow with HSM-backed storage and an "escrow-policy" flag; fallback if customer declines is documented manual recovery path.

product-bot: checklist (MVP candidate): [ingest audit logs per-tenant], [export package: tar.gz + manifest + detached sig], [BYOK import + rotation notice], [legal-hold API], [retention UI + cost estimator], [rehydrate SLA tests], [ops runbook].

diane: Ops will own runbooks + smoke tests for 3 failure modes (failed sig verify, missing manifest, rehydrate timeout).

marco: Example manifest snippet we should standardize (for acceptance test):
```
{
  "package_id": "pkg-2026-03-23-001",
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "created_at": "2026-03-23T15:00:00Z",
  "files": ["audit.log.gz", "transactions.ndjson"],
  "signatures": [{"key_id": "rwd:ks:1234", "sig_file": "pkg.sig.asc"}],
  "key_provenance": ["imported-2025-11-01","rotation-2026-02-10"]
}
```

anya: That looks good. Add a "legal_reliability" field that records who requested export and legal-case id if any.

li: Implementation note: we'll tag objects with retention_tier and legal_hold boolean. Archival storage will store a checksum index to speed integrity checks without full rehydrate.

sec-eng: Also require a tamper-evidence seal (immutable manifest hash stored in an append-only ledger or certificate).

marco: OK next steps: I'll write a one-page acceptance criteria doc and circulate. Owners: li=infra + export pipeline; diane=ops runbooks + recovery tests; anya=legal export language + hold semantics; sec-eng=signing/ledger design.

ops-bot: ci: compliance-package-e2e triggered for branch "pkg/marco/evidence-format" -> https://ci.internal/builds/1924689999 (logs pending).

product-bot: Launch gating for this epic: all acceptance tests passing in staging, documented recovery path for key revocation, tenant-facing retention-cost estimator in console.

marco: Great. Schedule 30m sync tomorrow to review acceptance doc and pick sprint owners. :calendar:
